messages:
morgan: Heads-up — I want to propose a different approach for the late-telemetry recompute we ran yesterday. The naive replay is costing too much and causing noisy routing thrash. Thinking about a snapshot-based incremental replay + tenant-aware quota smoothing.

liam: can you sketch the snapshot flow? is this like checkpoint+delta?

morgan: yeah — create a validated daily snapshot of aggregates (t=00:00) and only replay deltas since that snapshot. For late events we replay to a temporary diff-store, run the aggregate recompute locally, then merge if the delta passes quality checks. Means much less work for steady-state tenants.

anya: from console/UX side we need two things: a) an estimate of token/compute cost before starting (so operators can choose quota buckets) and b) a dry-run mode with preview diffs surfaced in the telemetry dashboard. We can add a modal that shows "estimated slots, expected delta rows, and projected cost".

natalie: quota smoothing is crucial — yesterday some small tenants got preempted when a few tenants spiked. Proposal: linearized lease smoothing where we spread a tenant's replay across N windows proportional to size, and cap concurrency per-parked-slot. Also add a soft-priority band for critical customers.

raj: routing note — we should respect route policies. I'd add an X-Replay-Priority header on replay requests so the serving/router can prefer cheaper model variants or route to dedicated pools if flagged critical. Also fallback policy: if the selected pool is saturated, route to queued backlog rather than fall back to hosted expensive path.

liam: re dedupe and correctness — how do we avoid double counting with overlapping snapshots and late events?

morgan: plan is to use event versioning + idempotent merge with tombstone windows. Pseudo: generate per-tenant sequence windows, each delta has a [start_seq,end_seq] and we only merge ranges that are monotonic. If overlap detected, the diff-store runs a reconciliation pass that computes the immutable key set and rejects merges with gaps.

anya: what about UX for operators to drill into rejected merges? Need a link from the replay job in console to a small error explorer with examples, sample offending events, and a "recompute candidate" preview.

natalie: can we also add a soft quota buffer for retries? e.g., have a quota reserve of 10% for replays so retries don't push others into preemption. This can be toggled per-org in the console.

ops-bot: deploy-batch-queue: scheduled job runner will pick up new replay workflow 'snapshot-incremental-v1' at 03:00 UTC.

raj: small CLI for ops to run dry-run:
```bash
ri-backfill run --mode=dry-run \\n  --from-snapshot=2026-03-20T00:00Z \\n  --to=2026-03-20T23:59Z \\n  --shards=16 \\n  --tenant=acme-corp \\n  --priority=soft
```

liam: we should also add a synthetic-hash test to the dry-run to surface distribution skews (runs 10k sampled events through the routing decisions). That would have caught yesterday's hotspot.

morgan: agreed — include a sample-run option that emits a histogram to the replayer dashboard (heatmap by shard and predicted slot usage).

anya: for the dashboard, I'll add three new widgets on the replay page: 1) estimated cost (USD), 2) predicted slot occupancy over time, 3) preview diffs (top 10 changed aggregates). Also an acceptance toggle: "auto-merge if diff < 0.1%".

natalie: auto-merge threshold sounds fine but require an audit log entry and per-org opt-in. Also we should surface a compliance snapshot (hash+signature of snapshot) for Private deployments.

morgan: operational checklist I'm going to follow:
- open PR to add X-Replay-Priority header and console flag (migrate routing table to accept header)
- implement snapshot delta algorithm + idempotent merge in replayer
- add dry-run CLI and synthetic-hash test
- add replay preview widgets and cost estimator in console
- enable quota smoothing reserve (10% default) with per-org toggle

liam: ping me when you open the PR, I can look at the merge logic.

anya: I'll draft the console mocks — want an operator flow for 'preview -> dry-run -> approve -> schedule'.

morgan: cool. I'll open an RFC and a tiny spike branch with the delta store prototype today. If we can get a dry-run and dashboard preview in the next 48h we can run a canary for a handful of tenants.

raj: one more: metrics & alerts — add a "replay-diff-regression" alert when post-merge aggregates change >X% vs snapshot on >5 consecutive keys, and a routing-saturation alert when fallback rate >5% for more than 5 minutes.

morgan: noted. final question for the thread — any objections to starting the canary on Wed 2026-03-24 03:00 UTC using 5 tenants (mix of small/med/critical)?

natalie: fine by me, will inform customer success about potential brief divergence in metrics.

liam: +1

anya: +1, I'll prepare the console flow and label the job UI as 'canary'.

morgan: awesome — thanks. I'll drop PR/links here when ready. :thumbsup:
